title: Custom Programming Language Interpreter & AST Evaluator
problem: Software engineers interact with high-level programming languages daily, yet the underlying execution mechanisms—lexical tokenization, recursive descent parsing, abstract syntax tree construction, scope resolution, and virtual machine bytecode evaluation—remain opaque black boxes. Building an interpreter from first principles clarifies runtime language mechanics and domain-specific language design. This project implements a complete programming language engine in Go comprising a lexical scanner, a Pratt operator-precedence parser, an AST tree-walking evaluator with lexical closures, and an alternative stack-based bytecode compiler and virtual machine.
use_cases: Domain-specific configuration languages for enterprise rule evaluation engines
Sandboxed scripting runtimes for game development and plugin extensions
Interactive command-line query parsers for proprietary data structures
hard_parts: Implementing Pratt operator precedence parsing to handle complex infix, prefix, and postfix expressions cleanly
Preserving lexical closure state across first-class and higher-order functions without leaking scope bindings
Compiling nested control flow structures into linear bytecode instructions with relative jump address resolution
Optimizing virtual machine stack operations to minimize garbage collection allocations in hot execution loops
screener_signals: Modular Go implementation cleanly separating lexer, parser, AST nodes, compiler, and VM modules
Deterministic language test suite verifying 120 distinct syntax programs and edge cases
Anti-fake verification script accepting dynamic arithmetic and closure scripts via stdin and asserting output

stack.role: systems programming language for compiler, AST evaluator, and bytecode virtual machine

components.name: Lexical Scanner
components.purpose: Converts raw source code text into a structured stream of typed language tokens

components.name: Pratt AST Parser
components.purpose: Constructs an abstract syntax tree using top-down operator precedence parsing algorithms

components.name: AST Tree-Walking Evaluator
components.purpose: Evaluates AST nodes directly while managing lexical scope environments and closure captures

components.name: Bytecode Compiler & Stack VM
components.purpose: Translates AST into bytecode instructions and executes opcodes on an efficient stack virtual machine

components.name: Interactive REPL Interface
components.purpose: Provides interactive read-eval-print-loop shell for real-time expression evaluation and debugging

architecture.data_flow: Source code text enters the Lexical Scanner; tokens are emitted to the Pratt Parser; the parser constructs an Abstract Syntax Tree; for interpreted mode, the Tree-Walking Evaluator executes nodes within an Environment scope frame; for compiled mode, the Bytecode Compiler emits instructions and constant pools; the Stack Virtual Machine executes opcodes, manipulating the operand stack and returning output values.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Parser syntax error reporting halting execution upon invalid token sequences; runtime type assertions checking operand compatibility.

prerequisites: Intermediate Go programming (structs, interfaces, recursion, memory pointers)
Familiarity with fundamental data structures (stacks, hash maps, trees)
Basic knowledge of BNF or EBNF grammar notation

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU-bound compilation and interpretation)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external accounts, cloud dependencies, or API keys required
environment.fallback_path: AST tree-walking evaluator only if bytecode virtual machine module encounters platform-specific issues

riskiest_component.name: Lexical Closure Memory Leaks and Scope Mutation Races
riskiest_component.fallback: Implement immutable environment frames that copy outer references explicitly rather than sharing pointer references
